claim: Refined MDL (NML, Bayes mixture, prequential) charges about (k/2)log n bits for k parameters plus a geometry term; it behaves like BIC, so it is consistent but not prediction-optimal against AIC/CV.
agent_test: Compare complexity-penalised vs raw-fit tie-break among candidate hypotheses at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Under misspecification (all candidates wrong), plain MDL/Bayes can be inconsistent and pick over-complex models for all n; learning-rate eta<1 (SafeBayes) repairs it in the demonstrated regression case.
agent_test: Check whether a length-based tie-break prefers over-complex hypotheses when the true rule is outside the proposal set; add a damping weight on the complexity term.
audit_note: Content is accurate (suboptimal for all large n, not all n; SafeBayes eta about 0.4 repairs the regression case), but all listed sources are Grunwald's own group (Grunwald-Langford, Grunwald-van Ommen, Grunwald-Roos review) and the review merely summarises the other two; there is no independent replication in the evidence.

claim: Two-part codes with raw float32 weights are far worse than a uniform code (MNIST >8.6 Mbits, ratio >45; CIFAR10 >428 Mbits, ratio >2500); prequential coding is the tight code for deep nets (MNIST 4.10 kbits, ratio 0.02, 99.5% acc; CIFAR10 45.3 kbits, ratio 0.27).
agent_test: Score candidate explanations by prequential (predict-then-reveal) code length on the examples rather than by a description-plus-fit sum.

claim: Fake (random) labels cannot be compressed: code length stays near the uniform code even though networks can memorise them. Memorisation does not count as explanation under MDL.
agent_test: Reject a hypothesis whose fit to the examples needs as many bits to state as the examples themselves.
audit_note: Voita and Titov use control tasks (random tags per word type) and show larger model code, which supports but is not the same experiment as Blier and Ollivier's MNIST fake labels.

claim: Catch-up: big models have a worse cumulative prequential code than uniform until about 5,000 CIFAR samples (per-label cost below uniform after about 1,000); switching fixes it. Complexity penalties matter most with few examples.
agent_test: In few-example tasks, test whether a simple-first prior beats a flat tie-break.

claim: Description-length probing is more reliable than accuracy: accuracy gave the wrong verdict in 8 of 10 probe settings, MDL in none; layer-0 POS online code 96 kbits (linguistic) vs 515 (control) while accuracy was 93.7 vs 96.3; accuracy order of layers flips with seed (97.48/97.31 vs 97.38/97.48).
agent_test: When judging whether a reasoning step carries information, use code length with model cost counted, not accuracy on one run.

claim: Probe model cost reveals complexity: real-task probes prune to 33-75 neurons, control-task probes stay several times larger.
agent_test: Use the size of the explanation needed as a signal of whether the pattern is real.

claim: Language models are lossless compressors via arithmetic coding: Chinchilla 70B reaches 43.4% on ImageNet patches (PNG 58.5%), 16.4% on LibriSpeech (FLAC 30.3%), 8.3% on enwik9 (gzip 32.3%).
agent_test: Background for using LM log-probs as code lengths; not a scaffold test.

claim: Once parameter bytes are counted (two-part view), big LMs lose to gzip on 1 GB data: Chinchilla 1B about 211%, 7B about 1,400%, 70B about 14,000% of raw. An optimal model size exists per dataset size.
agent_test: Model-cost accounting matters: charge for scaffold and context length when comparing explanations.

claim: Average benchmark score is near-linear in bits per character on in-domain external text: Pearson about -0.95 per domain, -0.93 overall (RMSE 3.1%) over 31 LLMs and 12 benchmarks; weaker out of domain; limited to base models.
agent_test: Use per-token log-loss of a hypothesis on held-out items as a cheap proxy for its quality.
audit_note: Information Capacity follow-up (56 models) is a different measure and only loosely supports; the claim rests on Huang et al.

claim: Choosing in-context examples by minimum label code length lifts GPT2-XL accuracy: TopK+MDL 60.16 vs TopK 58.14 (+3.5% rel), random 42.78 to 43.06; the score reduces to model confidence. Small model, 8 datasets. No independent replication or newer-model test found (search blocked); the paper itself says TopK helps only on small-label NLU tasks.
agent_test: Replicate on a current model at equal tokens; check gain over a plain confidence tie-break.

claim: Rissanen Data Analysis: a feature is useful if it shortens online label code length (MNLI: word order halves label code vs 75% shuffled; CoLA incompressible without word order).
agent_test: Use as an ablation method for which scaffold parts help.

claim: Next-token loss over a context equals its prequential code length, so ICL trained on full sequences prefers simpler task explanations and beats train-risk ICL and regularised SGD at low data; the advantage vanishes with enough data.
agent_test: Prefer explanations fitted sequentially over the examples when examples are few.

claim: A large pretrained LLM (GPT-4/gpt-4o) did not minimise prequential code length on novel Mastermind tasks: much worse cross-entropy than small meta-trained ICL models and than a marginal-label baseline (5 seeds). Caveat: the gpt-4o run already used one-example-at-a-time sequential prediction, so forced sequencing is not the missing fix; the task (two-number feedback on 8-digit codes) may also be too hard in context.
agent_test: Do not assume the model's own plausibility judgement implements a simplicity prior; compute lengths explicitly or verify by sampling.

claim: MDL regularisation recovers hand-built perfect solutions on formal languages where L1/L2 fail (Dyck-1 MDL net |H|=139, test gap +0.1%; L1/L2 gaps up to 11-13%), but search for the MDL optimum is hard from random init.
agent_test: Small-model only; not transferable to LLM agents without further evidence.

claim: Pure MDL learners on ARC are verified but weak: MADIL fits 69 of 400 evaluation tasks and 57 are correct (82% generalisation, 180 s budget per task but 80% of solutions within 20 s; 59 correct under the all-test criterion vs Icecuber 117), while CompressARC gets 20.0% pass@2 on the 400 evaluation tasks (18.5% pass@1) with 76K parameters and no pretraining, at about 20.7 GPU-minutes per puzzle on an RTX 4070 (138 h total). Both generate their own candidates; neither was tested as a ranker of LLM-proposed programs in these papers.
agent_test: Use compression score as a ranker of candidate programs from an LLM, not as the generator.
audit_note: Numbers check out (MADIL 69 fit, 57 correct, 82%, 59 vs Icecuber 117 under the all-test criterion that also counts two tasks with a non-fitting model; CompressARC 20.0/18.5%, 76K, 138 h, about 20.7 min), but MADIL is described as efficient (80% of solutions within 20 s, 'greater efficiency'), so 'slow' applies only to CompressARC; 'stricter' count is a mislabel.
claim_before_audit: Pure MDL program learners on ARC are verified but weak and slow: MADIL fits 69 of 400 eval tasks and 57 are correct (82% generalisation, 180 s budget per task; 59 correct under the stricter all-test count vs Icecuber 117). CompressARC gets 20.0% pass@2 on the 400 eval tasks (18.5% pass@1) with 76K parameters and no pretraining, at about 20.7 GPU-minutes per puzzle on an RTX 4070 (138 h total). Both generate their own candidates; neither was tested as a ranker of LLM-proposed programs.

claim: Propose-and-verify with LLM priors: summarising hypotheses first lifts ARC from 17% (direct) to 23% (program) to 30% (summarised hypotheses), 33% human-selected; held-out validation selects correct programs, e.g. 100% at 200 examples where SGD stays near chance.
agent_test: Test choosing among N candidate rules by shortest-rule-that-fits vs first-fit at equal tokens.

claim: MDL-style aggregation of sampled outputs gives small, inconsistent gains: MIDGARD KELM 47.4 vs greedy 46.9, WebNLG 29.3 vs 29.1 (gpt-3.5), equal on KELM for Code-Llama.
agent_test: Compare with majority vote at equal samples; expect a small effect.

claim: MDL consolidation of LLM-proposed rules cuts rule count 7% to 20% while holding or raising accuracy (ToolHop 72 rules, BFCL 151). Caveat: compared only with LLM prompt-merging, not recency or usage pruning; unseen-split gains are +1.0 (ToolHop 42.1 to 43.1) and +0.9 (BFCL 47.6 to 48.5), below the reported SD of 1.2-1.6.
agent_test: Test pruning stored lessons by a length criterion at equal tokens.

claim: Exact two-part MDL over recurrences gives a contamination-free difficulty score: discovery point matches the identifiability bound in 89% of cases and correlates with structural size (r=+0.85), not growth (r=-0.007).
agent_test: Use rule size as a difficulty gauge.

claim: LLMs asked for the shortest program for a sequence do poorly: at length 128 GPT-4o gets 35.6 / 15.0 / 29.6 / 24.8 / 6.5 / 33.3 percent accuracy (Audio-16, Audio-8, MFCC, DNA, Text, Synthetic), Llama-3.1-405B 18.0 / 10.1 / 24.2 / 22.5 / 9.6 / 18.0; programs are longer than gzip (precision 1.5-3.2). A trained 1.5B SeqCoder reaches 36-84%.
agent_test: Do not ask the model to minimise length directly; compute length externally.

claim: MDL and validation-style scores depend on dataset size, so representation rankings can flip as data grows; MDL measures only one slice of the loss-data curve.
agent_test: Check rank stability of the tie-break at different example counts.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: MDL gives a non-vacuous generalisation bound for GPT-2 124M only with SubLoRA compression: 12.12 bits per dim vs 70.76 original (vacuous) and 15.62 random guess.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Deep-net generalisation despite perfect fit has only a qualitative MDL explanation (flat minima need fewer bits); no measured test.
agent_test: None.

claim: Among programs that fit all training pairs, about 9% are false positives on ARC (Li et al. 2024), and majority vote over their test outputs already removes about half of the problems that have one. Programs correct on all examples almost always generalise (Hypothesis Search). So the room for a length tie-break after verification and vote is small.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare first-fit, majority vote, confidence and shortest-fit on the fit-but-disagree cases only; count how often the tie-break changes the answer.

claim: With few examples, spurious expressions that fit training pairs but fail on test are MADIL's main generalisation failure (21 training tasks), and 21 of 62 search failures need non-compressive steps. The authors say the data-versus-model weight needs revising.
agent_test: Sweep a complexity weight (including eta below 1) on rule-induction tasks with 2 to 5 examples and measure held-out accuracy.

claim: Fit-only selection over many LLM hypotheses can overfit the exemplars (MiniSCAN: T=3 N=1 beat N=5), and plain sampling plus majority vote does not reliably help rule induction, while hypotheses plus symbolic execution does.
agent_test: Keep one hold-out example out of the fit and use it as the first tie-break before any length rule.

claim: Bits per character is tokenizer-normalised in Huang et al. and held across 31 base models, but raw compression rates in Deletang et al. change with tokenizer and model size in opposite directions (ASCII 6.4 percent at 38M parameters beats the largest BPE row). Only within-model comparisons are safe.
agent_test: If bits per character is used inside a run, fix one model and tokenizer and compare candidates only against each other.

claim: Hewitt and Liang's control tasks (random labels per word type) show a high-capacity probe reaches 92.8 control accuracy vs 71.2 for a linear probe on the same representation, with equal task accuracy (97.3 vs 97.2). Capacity hides whether a representation holds the information, the idea MDL probing later formalised.
agent_test: A cheap scrambled-label check on a candidate rule: if it fits scrambled examples as well, treat the fit as uninformative.

claim: Rissanen 1978 introduced two-part codes on discretised countable sets with the complexity term approximated as zero (per Gruenwald and Roos 2019). The primary paper was not opened.
agent_test: None.
